biography.ja: アメリカ・トレントンに生まれ、ナディア・ブーランジェに師事した。1920年代のパリで、飛行機のプロペラ音や複数の自動演奏ピアノを用いた過激な前衛作品で物議を醸し、「アメリカの不良少年」の異名を取った。後年はハリウッドで映画音楽の作曲家として活動する一方、女優ヘディ・ラマーと共同で魚雷の誘導技術に応用可能な通信技術の特許を取得した、発明家としての顔も持つ。
biography.en: Born in Trenton, in the United States, he studied under Nadia Boulanger. In 1920s Paris he caused a sensation with radical avant-garde works using airplane propeller sounds and multiple synchronized player pianos, earning him the nickname "the bad boy of music." In his later years he worked as a film composer in Hollywood, while also holding a patent, developed together with the actress Hedy Lamarr, for a communication technology applicable to torpedo guidance, giving him a second identity as an inventor.

style.ja: 初期の代表作では、通常の管弦楽編成を離れ、機械的な騒音や打楽器的な反復リズムを大胆に取り入れ、音楽と工業社会のイメージを直結させる過激な実験を行った。後年はより穏健な新古典主義的語法へ転じ、ハリウッドで培った実用的な作曲技術を演奏会用作品にも生かした。
style.en: In his early landmark work he departed from a conventional orchestral ensemble, boldly incorporating mechanical noise and percussive, repetitive rhythm to make a radical experiment linking music directly with the imagery of an industrial society. In his later years he turned to a more moderate neoclassical idiom, bringing the practical compositional skills he honed in Hollywood into his concert works as well.

impact.ja: 機械的な騒音を作曲の素材とする発想は、後にケージが探求した音そのものへの関心と並べて語られることがある。音楽家でありながら通信技術の特許を持つという異色の経歴は、芸術と科学技術の垣根を越えた人物として広く語り継がれ、その特許は後年の無線通信技術の先駆けとして再評価されている。
impact.en: His idea of using mechanical noise as compositional material is sometimes discussed alongside Cage's later interest in sound itself. His unusual career, a musician who also held a technology patent, is widely retold as an example of a figure who crossed the boundary between art and science, and his patent has since been reassessed as a forerunner of later wireless communication technology.
